disposition_reason: Table 2 prints mean ± SD As, Cd, Cr, Cu, Hg, Ni, Se and Zn in tomato fruit from two wastewater-irrigated sites in Ouagadougou, alongside soil and wastewater.

study.design: Field survey of wastewater-irrigated tomato at two peri-urban production sites, with soil and wastewater
study.origin: Boulmiougou and Kossodo production sites, Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso (near industry; tannery near Kossodo)

period.as_reported: harvest at the end of October 2018

study.method: HNO3/HClO4/H2SO4 (5:1:1) digestion of 1 g dry sample at 80 C; graphite furnace AAS (Shimadzu 6800, GFA 7000)

findings.integrity_flag: Every tomato value in Table 2 equals about 0.87 x the Boulmiougou soil value for the same metal, and Table 3 transfer factors are 0.86-0.87 for all eight metals; identical soil-to-fruit ratios across metals are not consistent with independent measurements. Mercury at about 15 mg/kg dry weight in tomato is also implausible.
findings.notes: Fruit hand-harvested end of October 2018 from wastewater-irrigated plots near industry; washed, dried at 105 C, powdered; tri-acid digestion; graphite furnace AAS (Shimadzu 6800/GFA 7000). Table unit printed as mg/kg (or per litre for wastewater); basis dry. Number of fruits/plants not stated.

unresolved: Tomato values are a constant fraction of soil values for every metal at each site (0.87 and 0.80), so transfer factors are identical across metals; the data may be derived rather than measured. All tomato findings flagged.
Section 3.4 text gives Kossodo tomato Cu and Ni as 133.56 and 72.70, which are the Kossodo wastewater values, and calls Cr "2.71-2.78", which are the Cd values.
Table 5 microbial results are titled "lettuce" although the study is on tomato.
Lead was not measured although the manifest and limits mention it.
Wastewater values are labelled mg/kg or per litre in the same table; not extracted (not food).

regulatory_or_exposure.what: FAO/WHO limits for tomato as cited by the authors
